main_mystery: What happened the summer Mara was 8 that made her split herself and forget?
truth: Mara witnessed her mother Lydia push her lover Alain Dubois off the attic walkway after he threatened to expose their affair. Alain fell through the weakened floor clutching Mara's one-eyed bear (Wick) and died. Lydia forced Mara to swear secrecy, and Mara's psyche fractured, creating a silent child-self (the Girl in Blue) who trapped the memory in the bear. The child now waits for Mara to reclaim the bear so she can remember and become whole.

red_herrings.description: Mara finds a newspaper clipping about a child disappearing from the neighborhood the summer she stayed at the house, leading her to suspect the house is haunted by that missing child.
red_herrings.purpose: Misdirect away from the true nature of the Girl in Blue

red_herrings.description: Gerald tells Mara that Aunt Ilse committed suicide in the attic, making her fear the house's past is violent and that the girl might be Ilse's ghost.
red_herrings.purpose: Misdirect toward Ilse as victim and away from Mara's own trauma

red_herrings.description: Mara uncovers a locked room filled with old religious artifacts and an inverted cross, hinting at a supernatural exorcism having been performed in the house.
red_herrings.purpose: Misdirect toward a demonic explanation, away from the psychological truth

major_reveals.description: The Girl in Blue is not a ghost but a projection of Mara's own abandoned childhood self, created when her psyche fractured.
major_reveals.impact: Shifts the mystery from external haunting to internal psychological fracture; establishes that the girl is tied to Mara's past.

major_reveals.description: The one-eyed bear (Wick) is a psychometric memory anchor: holding it triggers forgotten memories of the traumatic event.
major_reveals.impact: Confirms the mechanism of the mystery; identifies the bear as the key to recovering the lost summer.

major_reveals.description: Mara's mother Lydia pushed her lover Alain Dubois from the attic walkway, and Mara witnessed the fall and subsequent cover-up.
major_reveals.impact: Reveals the core event; Lydia is unmasked as the perpetrator; the why of the split becomes clear.

major_reveals.description: The full memory integrates: Mara understands she created the Girl in Blue to survive the trauma and that holding Wick in the attic will complete the reintegration. The second shadow is the child-self approaching merger. Mara must choose to become whole or remain fractured.
major_reveals.impact: Complete resolution of the central mystery; sets up the final choice in chapter 10 and the series hook regarding Aunt Ilse.

clues.description: Mara notices the Girl in Blue only appears when Wick (the bear) is in the room; when she moves the bear to another room, the child vanishes.
clues.note: First hint that the girl and the bear are linked.

clues.description: Mara catches the Girl in Blue mimicking her own hand gestures exactly, like a mirror without the motion delay.
clues.note: Suggests the girl is a projection of Mara herself.

clues.description: When Mara first handles Wick, she experiences a brief flash of a woman screaming and a wooden floor cracking, but cannot hold the image.
Asher discovers an old diary entry by Aunt Ilse that describes the bear as 'the keeper of what must not be remembered until the bearer is ready.'
clues.note: Confirms the bear's role as a deliberate memory anchor.

clues.description: The bear's one glass eye, when held up to cold moonlight, reflects a blurred image of the attic walkway as seen from below.
clues.note: Visual proof that the bear stores a specific visual memory.

clues.description: Mara finds a child's drawing (her own, aged 8) hidden behind a loose floorboard: a red-haired woman pushing a man off a ledge while a small girl watches from behind a curtain.
clues.note: Direct witness evidence drawn by Mara herself.

clues.description: During a phone call with Lydia, Mara confronts her about the summer; Lydia snaps, 'That man was ruining our family. I did what had to be done. You promised you'd forget.'
clues.note: Verbal admission of guilt and of Mara's repressed promise.

clues.description: Mara finds a locket under the attic floorboards containing a photograph of Lydia and Alain Dubois, dated the summer of her stay.
clues.note: Proof of the affair and that Alain was present in the house.

clues.description: Neighbor Gerald admits to Asher that he heard a crash and a woman's scream on the last night of Mara's visit, but kept quiet because Lydia paid him.
Mara realizes she has always avoided her reflection in dark windows; the Girl in Blue never appears in mirrors at all.
clues.note: Hints at the psychological split and the child's non-separate nature.

clues.description: The second shadow Mara sees at the edge of her vision grows larger and moves closer every time she makes progress remembering; it now takes a childlike shape.
clues.note: Visual metaphor for the approaching reintegration.

clues.description: Mara deciphers a final entry in Aunt Ilse's journal: 'The child split to survive. The bear holds the death. Only when she holds it in the attic where it happened will she see the whole. I have kept it ready for her.'
clues.note: Full explanation of the mechanism and the aunt's role.
